script_old: Even McDonald's can lose trademark protection when it can't prove the right kind of use. This is the European Union's General Court, in June twenty twenty-four. In the EU, a registered trademark can be revoked for goods or services where it hasn't been genuinely used over a five-year period. McDonald's Big Mac registration covered more than burgers. It also listed things like chicken sandwiches, foods made from poultry, and services for operating restaurants. A challenge was brought, and the court looked at the evidence from twenty twelve to twenty seventeen. For chicken sandwiches, McDonald's had advertising posters, a TV ad and some social media screenshots. But the court said the evidence didn't show the extent of the mark's use for chicken sandwiches: how much, how often, how regularly. So that part was revoked, along with poultry foods. For restaurant services, the court said using Big Mac for a meat sandwich can't prove use for running restaurants. So that part went too. But the burger side survived. Protection for meat sandwiches, and related sandwich and meat food categories, stayed in place. So this wasn't McDonald's losing the Big Mac.
